summary: The main article describes a nickel/photoredox-catalyzed method for the direct carbamoylation of (hetero)aryl bromides using dihydropyridines. It includes one table for optimization studies and three figures detailing the scope of substrates and the proposed reaction mechanism, along with one scheme for the synthesis of the radical precursor.

items.heading: Figure 1. The presented radical cross-coupling approach to amide synthesis under photoredox-nickel dual catalysis.
items.description: This figure illustrates the general dual-catalytic strategy for the synthesis of amides from aryl bromides and dihydropyridines.

items.heading: Scheme 1. Synthesis of the carbamoyl radical precursor 1 ; AcOH: acetic acid; DCM: dichloromethane.
items.description: Shows the synthetic route for preparing the carbamoyl radical precursor 1 from amino crotonate and glyoxylic acid.

items.heading: Table 1. Optimization studies and control experiments.
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of reaction conditions, including solvents and control experiments, for the cross-coupling reaction.

items.heading: Figure 2. Scope of (hetero)aryl bromides.
items.description: This figure displays the substrate scope of various (hetero)aryl bromides used in the carbamoylation process.

items.heading: Figure 3. Scope of carbamoyl radical precursors.
items.description: This figure shows the scope of different carbamoyl radical precursors, including various amino acid derivatives and secondary/tertiary amides.

items.heading: Figure 4. Proposed mechanism.
items.description: This figure depicts the proposed catalytic cycle involving nickel and photoredox catalysis for the amide synthesis.
